title: Fit an O-ring onto a hydraulic plug: stretch it over the thread by no more than 50%, seat it square and untwisted
instruction: Fit the O-ring into the groove at the base of the plug's thread.
context: Hydraulic and pipe fitters and mobile heavy equipment mechanics (O*NET 47-2152.00, 49-3042.00) fit O-rings onto straight-thread O-ring boss (ORB) fittings and plugs, whose ring sits in a groove between the thread and the hex. The ring is stretched only as far as it takes to pass over the thread, carried down square to the groove and let close into it, then checked seated all the way round. Seal makers limit installation stretch to 50%: past it the ring's section thins for good and the joint weeps. A ring pushed or rolled down the thread instead of stretched over it twists, and a twisted ring left in the groove spirals and leaks. A ring let go tilted leaves one side on the thread, where it is cut when the plug is screwed into its port. Here it is the AS568-924 90-durometer FKM ring of a -24 (1.875 inch thread) boss plug.
setup: Positions are in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, with x forward, y to the robot's left and the table top at z 0. A blue anodized aluminum bench holder 9 x 9 x 4 cm is fixed to the table, centered at x 34, y -10. Standing hex-down on it on the axis x 34, y -10 is a zinc-plated steel SAE J1926 -24 O-ring boss hex plug: a 2.25 inch (57.15 mm across flats) hex from z 4.0 to 5.4, then the O-ring groove (undercut) 3.6 mm long with a 44.2 mm diameter from z 5.4 to 5.76, its lower wall the hex face, then the 1.875-12 UN thread, 47.6 mm across the crests, from z 5.76 up to the plug's flat end face at z 7.66 with a 1.5 mm chamfer. The O-ring is an AS568-924 bright blue 90-durometer fluorocarbon (FKM) O-ring, 43.7 mm inside diameter with a 3.0 mm section; it lies flat and centered on the plug's end face (z 7.66 to 7.96). Nothing else is on the table; both arms start at their home poses with the grippers open.
scoring: The ring's stretch is its inner circumference: the loop round the two fingertips that hold it and, once both are outside the thread, round the thread too. Over-stretch: if the ring's inside diameter ever exceeded 65.5 mm (50% stretch, seal makers' installation limit for this FKM, half its 100% minimum elongation) its section has thinned for good and the score is 0, irreversible. Seated means the ring lies in the groove closed onto its 44.2 mm bottom, no fingertip is in it or pressing on it, and it did not land tilted: let go (also when one fingertip leaves it before the other) with the fingertips' height difference over their spacing more than 4 degrees off square, the 50 mm ring's far side sits 3.5 mm off the groove plane, more than its 3.0 mm section, and lands on the thread. Not seated: 0. Twist: a ring pushed along the thread without being stretched clear of it rolls, 38 degrees per mm; only a fingertip arriving on the ring's near face pushes it, and a ring in the groove does not roll; seated with more than 90 degrees of roll left in it (a quarter turn, 2.4 mm of rolling; its parting line is on its face, visibly spiraling) scores 0. Seated, untwisted and never over-stretched: 0.9, raised to 1.0 when both arms are also back home and still (tool points within 3 cm of their start). Possible scores: 0, 0.9, 1.0. A real trial is checked from the top video (finger spacing against a mm scale on the holder), by eye and fingertip round the ring (fully in the groove, parting line straight), and by measuring the ring's section with calipers after the trial.
reset_notes: Roll the ring out of the groove with a plastic O-ring pick (never a metal one), check its section is still 3.0 mm with calipers and its parting line straight, and replace it if not (rings are cheap and over-stretched ones are scrapped). Lay it flat and centered on the plug's end face.
fidelity: The ring has no contact simulation: its position along the plug, stretch and twist are a model driven by the gripper's fingertips (it slides only when stretched clear of the thread, closes into the groove when let go over it). It is treated as stretched evenly round; a real ring held at two points ovals and rubs the thread between them. Pushed down unstretched, it rolls without slipping; its tilt is the fingertips' height difference. It has no collision shape; the plug and holder do.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 (2,400 steps, max_steps); demo: 1.0 (339 steps)
